title: Journeeze catalog bundle, version 1
description: The one versioned, Journeeze-owned format a product sends Journeeze: its catalog (personas, jobs with steps and desired outcomes, Jevitate journeys verbatim with their links), demo media manifests, check results with machine baselines, and machine findings (docs/contract/catalog-bundle-v1.md). A bundle is `bundle.json` (this document) plus the media files it lists, as a directory or a ZIP with `bundle.json` at its root. The whole bundle is validated before anything is written. It never carries real typed values, query strings, credentials or personal data. This schema is v1.1 (minor 1 adds `finding.locator` and `check.appVersion`): a reader prunes unknown fields only from a bundle whose `minor` is greater than its own (contract § Versioning).

version.description: The major version. A reader refuses any other major.

minor.description: The minor version. Minors only add optional fields; this schema is minor 1 (minor 0 plus `finding.locator` and `check.appVersion`).

catalogId.description: A catalog id (persona, job, job step, desired outcome): Jevitate's id rule, 1-64 of [A-Za-z0-9._-] starting alphanumeric. Maps to jz_domain::catalog::{PersonaId, JobId, JobStepId, OutcomeId}.

jevitateId.description: A bare Jevitate journey id (`metadata.id`). Lowercased, it is the journey slug in the product (jz_domain::JourneySlug); it MUST equal the `journeyId` the host sets on the journey's pages.

anchorName.description: A named anchor on a journey step (jz_domain::catalog::AnchorName). `job_start` and `job_end` are reserved for metric references and refused as anchor names.

anchorRef.description: Where a metric or a baseline point measures: an anchor name, or the reserved `job_start` / `job_end` (jz_domain::catalog::AnchorRef).

targetId.description: A Jevitate run target id (`result.target.id`, `explore --target`): 1-64 of [A-Za-z0-9_.-]. Check results are keyed on it, never on a start URL.

commit.description: A git commit id (abbreviated or full, lowercase hex).

routeTemplate.description: A path or route template within the app (`/settings/sites`, `/projects/{projectId}/board`), as in journey-candidates.v1.json: no scheme, host, query string, fragment or record id.

noPersonalData.description: Refuses text that looks like personal data: an email address, or a run of 9 or more digits (phone, account or card numbers).

noUrls.description: Refuses text that contains a URL (`://`, or `www.`).

noRecordIds.description: Refuses values that embed a record id: a UUID, 8 or more hex characters including a digit, or 6 or more digits.

catalogText.description: Repo-authored catalog text (job story, step name, outcome object): one printable, non-blank line with no personal data. The length bound is set where it is used.

machineText.description: Producer-written text (guide captions, finding observations): one printable line, no personal data, no URL, no record id. Written by the producer, never copied from a page or a typed value.

tool.description: `jevitate` (export / connect), `journeeze` (the board's download, re-uploaded), `custom` (a product's own exporter, e.g. a CI step).

name.description: The exporter's name; required when `tool` is `custom`.

commit.description: The product repository commit the catalog was read at (not the tool's own build). Recorded per connection as the last imported commit.

catalogPath.description: The catalog path in the repository (`.jevitate/` by default, or a namespace folder).

connection.description: A hint naming the repository the catalog came from (ADR 0016 `RepoRef` + catalog path). Never authority: the upload credential decides the product and connection.

name.description: The product's name in Journeeze. A guard: import refuses a bundle whose name differs from the product the upload credential belongs to.

channel.description: How the approval was given (Jevitate `approval.provenance.channel`). Informational: Journeeze decides approved/stale by recomputing the hash.

approval.description: A Jevitate approval: the content hash that was approved. Journeeze recomputes the entry's hash; equal = approved, different = stale, absent = draft (jz_domain::catalog::Approval).

otherFields.description: Any other descriptive keys of the persona's `personas.json` entry, verbatim, so the content hash recomputes. Journeeze never stores or shows them. Session keys (`storageState`, `login`) are never exported (they are outside the hash).

persona.description: A persona (executor role), from `.jevitate/personas.json`. Maps to jz_domain::catalog::Persona.

metric.description: One of the closed metric kinds over anchors and in-app answers (jz_domain::catalog::Metric; jtbd-data-model.md §3). Each kind carries exactly its own fields. Whether `from`/`to`/`at` name an anchor some journey of the job has is a catalog rule (a gap, never an error).

target.description: What good enough is (jz_domain::catalog::OutcomeTarget). A percent is at most 100. A unit that does not fit the metric is a catalog warning, not a refusal.

step.description: The job step it is about; absent = the whole job.

priority.description: Absent imports as `medium` (the domain requires one).

extensions.description: Namespaced tool-specific fields (jtbd-data-model.md §7.3), verbatim for the hash. Journeeze v1 reads none of them.

persona.description: Jevitate's legacy single persona (folded into `personas` on import).

storageState.description: Jevitate test-campaign field, verbatim for the hash (a path, never the file). Ignored on import.

goal.description: Jevitate test-campaign field, verbatim for the hash. Ignored on import.

success.description: Jevitate test-campaign field. Ignored on import.

preconditions.description: Jevitate test-campaign field. Ignored on import.

mutates.description: Jevitate test-campaign field. Ignored on import.

order.description: Jevitate test-campaign field. Ignored on import.

job.description: A job, exactly as its `.jevitate/jobs.json` entry (Jevitate 0.9 fields plus the optional jtbd-data-model.md §3 fields), so its content hash recomputes. Maps to jz_domain::catalog::Job.

typedValues.description: Walks a verbatim Jevitate journey: every typed value Jevitate kept in clear (`{"redacted": false, "value": …}`) must pass noPersonalData. Values come from a seeded, synthetic tenant; real ones are refused.

journeyFile.description: The Jevitate journey file (`.jevitate/journeys/<id>.json`) byte-for-byte as JSON, so its review hash recomputes (crates/jz_host/src/jevitate_hash.rs). Opaque beyond the fields named here: Journeeze reads only the fields crates/jz_host/src/journey_import.rs reads, holds the rest in memory to check the hash, and never stores it.

step.description: The journey step, numbered from 1 over the recorded steps.

anchor.description: jz_domain::catalog::JourneyAnchor. A boundary marks a job step, so it needs `jobStep`.

serves.description: Desired-outcome ids of `job` this path is meant to move.

link.description: The journey's place in the catalog (jz_domain::catalog::JourneyCatalogLink). Where the journey's own metadata also names `job`, `persona` or anchors, they must agree (an import check).

catalog.description: A full snapshot of the product's catalog from one source at `producer.commit`. An entry missing from a later snapshot is marked removed upstream, never deleted.

path.description: Relative to the bundle root. The journey segment is the journey id.

file.description: One media file in the bundle. Every file in the archive is listed here exactly once, and every reference elsewhere names a listed path (import checks).

privacy.description: The producer's attestation, as in journey-candidates.v1.json: every screenshot and the video were masked under jz-mask-v1 (fails closed), and the run used a seeded, synthetic tenant.

renderedFrom.description: The journey review hash the demo was rendered from. Import refuses a demo whose hash is not the journey's approved hash (a demo of a stale or draft journey).

status.description: Only `jevitate demo approve` output is exported; drafts never become help.

demo.description: The demo media manifest of one journey: the guide (`guide.md` steps), screenshots, video and subtitles. Replaces reading Jevitate's demo folder layout.

atMs.description: Milliseconds from the run's first step to the anchor's step completing.

baseline.description: The machine baseline (jtbd-data-model.md §5): when a clean replay reached each anchor. Time between two anchors is the floor for a `duration` outcome.

appVersion.description: Minor 1. The app's release/version label the check ran against (`commit` stays the build identity). Stored with the journey proof next to the commit, so machine and human time compare for the same release.

journeyHash.description: The journey review hash the run replayed. A failure on the approved hash marks the guide Stale; a clean run on it records "last proven".

outcome.description: Jevitate's canonical MissionOutcome, plus `pending-review` (a self-heal proposal awaits a person).

exitCode.description: The item's exit code; fixed by the outcome.

check.description: One check result, keyed by (target.id, commit, runId). Append-only evidence.

fingerprint.description: Jevitate's 16-hex finding fingerprint (defects, hangs); for UX findings, the contract's derived fingerprint (§ Findings). The finding's identity; the issue marker.

claim.description: The UX claim type (Jevitate `ClaimType`). `other` + `producerClaim` for a type this version does not know.

box.description: The implicated element's box on the screenshot, in CSS pixels.

finding.description: A machine finding: machine evidence, never human feedback. No on-screen quotes are exported (they may hold personal data).

element.description: The element, named for a person (`the "Save" button`): one printable line, no URL, no personal data.

fix.description: The suggested fix, one line with no URL scheme or host (`add data-testid="save-contact" to the "Save" button on /contacts/new`). The finding's `recommendation` repeats it.

steps.description: How many steps (across journeys) use the element.

locator.description: Minor 1. A brittle locator's suggested fix (Jevitate `LocatorSuggestion`): one finding per element (route + role + name), however many steps use it, so Journeeze files one issue per fix. Required iff the finding is `kind: ux`, `claim: other`, `producerClaim: locator-brittle`; refused on every other finding.
